goal: Add conservative complexity-aware review selection: Codex records a risk assessment, small documentation-only routine changes may use Sonnet, and uncertain, medium/high, sensitive or integration work uses Opus without quota-based fallback.

review.reason: This complete harness feature changes the reviewer trust policy, frozen model selection, integrity and saved-evidence validation; it requires the stronger reviewer.

acceptance.description: Only a documented low-risk routine assessment and small regular-text documentation-only scope may select Sonnet. Missing/medium/high assessment, integration scope, runtime/security/tooling/configuration context, large scope and unusual changes select Opus. The current task brief remains reviewed.

Model selection is frozen from the committed policy, task and complete base/head diff; preparation and reports expose reasons. Run/status rederive selection and reject changed assessment/model evidence, mismatched CLI model or missing provenance. Valid historical fixed-policy runs retain their original model evidence.

The selected model is used once per explicit attempt; quota, unavailable model and execution failures stay INCOMPLETE without silently falling back. Existing stdin privacy, minimal reviewer environment, integrity/check validation, output limits and attempt bounds remain intact.

Meaningful routing and failure regressions pass, documentation distinguishes Codex semantic judgment from narrow deterministic guards, historical Sonnet/Opus results are accurate, and mobile/API/dependency code remains unchanged.
